quote: Conclusions: Both PROK2 and calprotectin were independently associated with focal organ involvement; however, PROK2 showed stage-related variation and calprotectin was not independently associated with disease stage.
summary: Serum PROK2 was higher in brucellosis and independently associated with focal organ involvement (AUC 0.807); an infection biomarker study, not UC.

quote: PPI networks and enrichment analysis verified that downstream genes S100P, ALOX5AP, PROK2, and PADI4 may collaboratively participate in immune response and inflammation regulation.
summary: PROK2 is listed as one of four downstream genes in a sleep apnea network analysis without a specific result.

quote: The OGD model in H9C2 cells confirmed specific upregulation of GPR97, PROK2, ALPL and PADI4.
summary: PROK2 was upregulated in blood in acute myocardial infarction datasets and in oxygen-glucose-deprived cardiomyocyte cells; not a UC study.

quote: Consistent with these observations, the mRNAs of SOCS family genes encoding the STAT signalling inhibitory proteins SOCS1, SOCS3 and CISH were marked by m6A, exhibited slower mRNA decay and showed increased mRNAs and levels of protein expression in Mettl3-deficient naive T cells.
summary: SOCS3 is one of three SOCS genes stabilized and increased in Mettl3-deficient T cells that failed to cause colitis; the study centers on METTL3.

quote: We conclude that Socs3 is an essential negative regulator of IL-23 signaling, inhibition of which constrains the generation of Th17 differentiation.
summary: Socs3-deficient T cells showed enhanced IL-23-driven Stat3 phosphorylation and Th17 generation, so SOCS3 restrains Th17 differentiation.

quote: SOCS3 regulates cytokine or hormone signaling usually preventing, but in some cases aggravating, a variety of diseases.
summary: Review of SOCS3 as a JAK/STAT3 inhibitor controlling immune homeostasis in infection and autoimmunity.

quote: These findings collectively indicate that SOCS3 is involved in repressing the M1 proinflammatory phenotype, thereby deactivating inflammatory responses in macrophages.
summary: Myeloid SOCS3 deletion enhanced M1 macrophage polarization and worsened LPS sepsis in mice, showing SOCS3 restrains macrophage inflammation.

quote: These data suggest that hyperactivation of STAT3 results in severe colitis and that CIS3 plays a negative regulatory role in intestinal inflammation by downregulating STAT3 activity.
summary: CIS3/SOCS3 is induced in DSS colitis and its blockade in transgenic mice caused stronger STAT3 activation and more severe colitis.

quote: Using the gp130(Y757F/Y757F) mouse model of gastric cancer, which carries a mutated gp130 cytokine receptor signaling subunit that cannot bind the negative regulator of cytokine signaling SOCS3 and is characterized by hyperactivation of the signaling molecules STAT1 and STAT3, we have provided genetic evidence that IL-11 promotes chronic gastric inflammation and associated tumorigenesis.
summary: SOCS3 appears only as the binding partner missing in gp130 mutant mice; the study concerns IL-11 and STAT3 in gastric tumors.

quote: Periarticular injection of CIS3 adenovirus drastically reduced the severity of arthritis and joint swelling compared with control groups.
summary: Overexpressing CIS3/SOCS3 by adenovirus strongly reduced arthritis severity in mice; an arthritis model, not colitis.

quote: Co-expression of a STAT inhibitor, SOCS3, blocked IFN-gamma-mediated MD-2 promoter activation.
summary: SOCS3 co-expression blocked IFN-gamma-driven MD-2 promoter activity in intestinal epithelial cells, which would limit LPS responsiveness.

quote: In mice (gp130Y757F/Y757F) deficient in SHP2 and SOCS3 binding, but presenting hyperactivation of STAT1/3, T cell recruitment and CCL5 expression was enhanced.
summary: SOCS3 is mentioned only as a binding site missing in gp130 mutant mice; the study focuses on IL-6 and STAT3.

quote: Moreover, SOCS3 may be involved in UC pathogenesis and the absence of SOCS3 seems critical for CRC progression.
summary: SOCS3 protein was examined in UC biopsies along with IL6 and p-STAT3, and its absence was linked to progression to colorectal cancer.

quote: Despite this loss of IL-21 functions, IL-21-induced STAT3 activation was unimpaired and induced normal Socs3 expression.
summary: Socs3 expression is only noted as normal in Irf4-deficient Th cells; the paper concerns IRF4 in Th17 development.

quote: Especially, suppressor of cytokine signaling-1 (SOCS1) and SOCS3 are strong inhibitors of JAKs, because these two contain kinase inhibitory region at the N-terminus.
summary: Review of SOCS1 and SOCS3 as regulators of helper T cell differentiation and T cell mediated inflammatory disease.

quote: Also, SOCS3 small interfering RNA knockdown partially compensates for the action of TGF-beta on Th17 cell development.
summary: TGF-beta inhibits SOCS3 to prolong STAT3 activation and promote Th17 cells, and SOCS3 knockdown mimics this, so SOCS3 restrains Th17 development.

quote: We also demonstrate that overexpression of SOCS-3, a protein known to inhibit STAT activation in response to IL-6, down-regulates IL-6-induced NF-kappaB activation and ICAM-1 expression.
summary: SOCS-3 overexpression in Caco2 intestinal epithelial cells reduced IL-6-induced NF-kappaB activation and ICAM-1 expression.

quote: Further study indicated that inhibition of STAT3 Tyr705 phosphorylation in SARS-CoV-2 infected and viral spike protein expressing epithelial cells did not induce SOCS3 and MCP-1 expression.
summary: SOCS3 induction in spike-expressing epithelial cells depends on STAT3 phosphorylation; a COVID study, not about colitis.

quote: The functional dependence of Ezh2 for Socs3 is further illustrated by the rescue experiments in which silencing of Socs3 restores macrophage activation and rescues autoimmune inflammation in macrophage/microglial Ezh2-deficient mice.
summary: Ezh2 loss raised Socs3 and attenuated DSS colitis, and silencing Socs3 restored macrophage activation and inflammation, so SOCS3 dampens inflammation.

quote: Our results further demonstrate that miR-196b-5p promotes stemness and chemoresistance of CRC cells to 5-fluorouracil via targeting negative regulators SOCS1 and SOCS3 of STAT3 signaling pathway, giving rise to activation of STAT3 signaling.
summary: SOCS3 is a target of miR-196b-5p in colorectal cancer cells, alongside SOCS1; the paper centers on the microRNA.

quote: Furthermore, the STAT3 regulated protein, SOCS3, is also constitutively expressed in Crohn's patients but not in healthy volunteers.
summary: SOCS3 is constitutively expressed in intestinal T cells from Crohn's disease patients but not healthy volunteers.

quote: Cytokine-inducible Src homology 2 (SH2)-containing protein (CIS), SOCS1, and SOCS3 proteins regulate cytokine signals that control the polarization of CD4+ T cells and the maturation of CD8+ T cells.
summary: Review of CIS, SOCS1 and SOCS3 as negative regulators of cytokine signaling in T cells and tumor immunity.

quote: In particular, SOCS1 and SOCS3 are potent inhibitors of JAKs and can play pivotal roles in inflammation, as well as in the development and progression of cancers.
summary: Review of SOCS1 and SOCS3 in inflammation and cancer development.

quote: By repressing expression of the negative regulator SOCS3 dependent on the transcription factor NF-κB, IL-1 increased the amplitude and duration of phosphorylation of the transcription factor STAT3 induced by TH17-polarizing cytokines, which led to an altered balance in the binding of STAT3 and STAT5 to shared consensus sequences in developing T cells.
summary: IL-1 represses SOCS3 expression via NF-kappaB in developing T cells, prolonging STAT3 signaling and favoring Th17 over iTreg cells.

quote: IPF-HLFs were found to significantly overexpress IL-6 receptor (IL-6R), suppressor of cytokine signaling 3 (SOCS3), phospho-STAT3-Y705 and phospho-Smad3 in comparison to N-HLFs
summary: SOCS3 was overexpressed in lung fibroblasts from idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis patients versus controls; not a UC study.
